sections.html:
Dothan is the seat of Houston County, in the southeast corner of Alabama about 20 miles west of the Georgia line and 16 miles north of Florida. The city limits also reach north into Henry County and northwest into Dale County, so the county of your parcel is a real question for sellers. Dothan is the eighth-largest city in the state, with 71,072 residents at the 2020 census, and it serves as the commercial hub for southeast Alabama, southwest Georgia and part of the Florida Panhandle.

The 2020 census found 30,115 households in 33,242 housing units, with 9.4% of units vacant. Homeowner vacancy was 2.2% and rental vacancy 8.2%, and the median age was 40.4.

Growth has continued in every census, though more slowly. About 19.3 percent of residents were 65 or older in 2020, and nearly a third of households were one person living alone. Many of those homes will change hands as owners downsize, move to family or pass away, and heirs often prefer a quick sale to managing a vacant house from far away.

Summers are hot and humid, winters mild, and rain falls all year, with August the wettest month at 6.17 inches on average. Snow is rare, though a significant event hit the city on January 21, 2025. Tornadoes are a recurring concern in spring, summer and fall. Dothan's tornado activity runs below the Alabama average but 79 percent above the national average.

  • Check roof condition and shingle age, since tornado and thunderstorm wind are a regular worry here.
  • Look for moisture under floors and in crawlspaces after heavy summer rain.
  • Keep records of any storm repairs and insurance claims for the buyer's agent or your closing agent.

The terrain is flat, with small hills sloping toward the Chattahoochee River to the east and the Gulf coastal plain to the south, so drainage problems are usually local to a lot rather than a whole area.

sections.h2: Ross Clark Circle and getting around
sections.html:
A bypass called Ross Clark Circle (State Route 210) rings the city and carries U.S. 84 on the north, U.S. 231 on the west and U.S. 431 on the east. Where a house sits relative to the Circle is a simple way to describe its location to a buyer.

Dothan has no interstate. The nearest, I-10, runs about 32 miles south. U.S. 84 goes east 55 miles to Bainbridge, Georgia, and U.S. 231 goes south 83 miles to Panama City, Florida. Dothan Regional Airport has Delta service, and the Wiregrass Transit Authority offers dial-a-ride rather than fixed routes. Most households rely on cars, so a driveway, a garage and the distance to the Circle all get weighed.

A mayor and a six-district board of commissioners run Dothan, with a city manager handling daily operations. Ordinances and permits come from the city. A seller with unpermitted work, such as an enclosed porch or a finished garage, should ask city staff what is required before listing. A buyer's inspector or lender may ask for permit records, and clearing an issue early costs less than clearing it under a closing deadline.

The deed is recorded with the probate office of the county where the parcel sits, and Alabama collects a recordation tax at that time. Alabama Code section 40-22-1 sets the tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, and a form stating the actual purchase price goes with the deed.

Because Dothan reaches into three counties, ask your closing agent to confirm the county before anything is signed. Most parcels are in Houston County, but a few are not.

Property tax in Alabama is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. A sale that closes in the fourth quarter should settle that bill on the closing statement.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
1. Confirm the county that holds your parcel.
  2. Gather the deed, the latest tax bill, any mortgage payoff statement and a list of known repairs.
  3. Decide who signs. Heirs spread across states may need to sign by mail.
  4. Ask for an offer, and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs and showings.
  5. Pick a closing agent to run the title search, clear liens and prepare the settlement statement.
  6. Record the deed, and receive your proceeds once the bill and any liens are paid.

The order barely changes whether the buyer uses a loan or cash, but the time between steps does. A loan adds an appraisal and underwriting. Cash does not, which is why the closing date can be set to fit a job move or a family timeline.

Many sellers in Dothan are managing an older house, an inheritance or a rental that has run its course. Others are leaving for work and cannot wait through months of showings.

  • Heirs spread across states who inherit a Dothan house they do not want to manage.
  • Landlords with units that need more work than the rent supports.
  • Owners with roof, plumbing or HVAC problems after years of deferral.
  • Sellers with timing pressure from a job move or a divorce.

A direct cash sale can take away showings, lender appraisals and repair requests. If you want to see what that looks like for your house, submit the form on this page.

Before you accept any offer, ask the buyer to put the closing date, the price and who pays for title work in writing. Compare that with a listing plan and decide which fits your calendar.

faqs.q: How many people live in Dothan?
faqs.a: Dothan had 71,072 residents at the 2020 census, making it the eighth-largest city in Alabama.
Dothan is the county seat of Houston County, and parts of the city extend into Dale and Henry counties. Confirm your parcel's county before you record a deed.
No. The nearest interstate is I-10, about 32 miles south. Dothan is served by U.S. 84, 231 and 431, which meet at Ross Clark Circle.

faqs.q: When are Dothan property taxes due?
faqs.a: Alabama property tax is due October 1 and is delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: What tax do I pay to record a deed in Dothan?
faqs.a: Alabama's recordation tax is 50 cents per $500 of value on the deed, paid to the probate office before recording. Your closing agent normally handles it.
